key_insight: SCALPEL adapts a medical LLM into an efficient image-text encoder and adds anatomy- and negation-aware alignment to improve medical vision-language matching.
clinical_relevance: This could improve retrieval, zero-shot classification, and visual question answering from radiology reports by reducing errors from laterality and negation confusion.
method: Clinical report contrastive fine-tuning turns a generative LLM into a more isotropic encoder.
Asymmetric alignment uses offline feature caching to reduce memory cost during training.
Anatomy-Negation Aware Objective penalizes mismatched image-text pairs with laterality or negation errors.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports state-of-the-art results on MIMIC-CXR, CheXpert, and IU X-Ray across cross-modal retrieval, zero-shot disease classification, and medical VQA.
watch_item: Performance gains depend on accurate handling of anatomical laterality and negation, so implementation quality and domain-specific evaluation remain important.
paper_title: SCALPEL: Semantic Cross-modal Alignment via LLM-Powered Encoder Learning for Medical Vision-Language Representation
